name: Callaway Gardens
unique: Thirteen thousand acres of gardens built by a textile family on worn out cotton land, with a butterfly conservatory, a lakeside beach, a zipline and a spring azalea bloom that runs for miles of trail.
buzz: The azaleas in late March are the pilgrimage and the beach and butterfly house carry families the rest of the year. Bikes are the way to cover it.

name: F.D. Roosevelt State Park
unique: Georgia's largest state park, built by the CCC on the Pine Mountain ridge, with a stone pool fed by a spring, cabins from the 1930s and a 23 mile trail along the crest.
buzz: The Liberty Bell pool and the stone cabins are the Depression era survivors people come to see. The ridge trail has real climbs.

name: Pine Mountain Scenic Highway
unique: A ridge road along the Pine Mountain crest with overlooks west into the valley, built as a Roosevelt era project and still the best drive in this part of the state.
buzz: The overlooks at sunset are the reason. Motorcycles and sports cars work it on weekends.

name: Harris County Courthouse Square
unique: A courthouse square in a town incorporated in 1828, with antebellum houses on the streets behind it and the Pine Mountain ridge on the horizon.
buzz: Ten minutes off the highway and much quieter than the Callaway entrance. A good leg stretch.

name: Hills and Dales Estate
dates: Tuesday to Saturday, spring to December
unique: A 1916 Italianate villa and terraced boxwood garden built by the Callaway family on a design by a Ferrell Gardens gardener, with hedges older than the house and a view over LaGrange.
buzz: The boxwood terraces are the reason gardeners make the trip. House tours are timed and the garden alone takes two hours.

name: Bellevue Historical Home
unique: A Greek Revival house with a two story portico on a hill over LaGrange, furnished with family pieces and open as a house museum run by the local historical society.
buzz: The portico and the original furnishings are the draw. Thirty minutes of tour and a good story about the family.

name: Biblical History Center
unique: A research center with a full scale replica of a first century Jewish village, a Roman soldier's quarters and an authentic garden tomb, used to teach daily life rather than doctrine.
buzz: The reconstructed village is far more detailed than expected, and the guides are archaeologists. Believers and sceptics both come away talking about it.

name: Troup County Archives and Legacy Museum
unique: A county archive and museum on Main Street with the textile mill records, family papers and photographs of a town built by five mills and the families that ran them.
buzz: The mill records are the deep end and staff will pull files for you. Free and quiet.

name: Strange LaGrange Walking Tour
unique: A guided downtown walk built around the odd, grim and unlikely stories of a mill town, from the cemetery on the hill to the buildings that changed hands in the middle of the night.
buzz: Guides tell it well and the route covers the historic district. Book ahead, it runs on set evenings.

name: Roosevelt's Little White House
unique: The small wooden house where Roosevelt came to take the warm springs and died in 1945, kept as it was that day, with his hand controlled car, his cane collection and the unfinished portrait in the room.
buzz: The unfinished portrait and the plainness of the house are what people remember. The museum next door covers polio and the New Deal without flinching.

name: Warm Springs Pools and Institute
company: Roosevelt Warm Springs Institute for Rehabilitation
unique: The stone pools where people came to soak in 88 degree mineral water long before Roosevelt, and where he built a polio treatment center that still operates on the same campus.
buzz: The old pools are empty now and the rims and columns remain, which is more affecting than a working spa would be. Tours explain the therapy.

name: Downtown Warm Springs
unique: A main street of 1920s storefronts built for the crowds that came to take the waters, with a hotel, a pool hall and shops that still trade in a town of under 500.
buzz: The old hotel and the storefronts are the picture. Most people come for the Little White House and stay an extra hour here.

name: Chattahoochee River at Franklin
unique: The Chattahoochee running the whole western edge of Heard County, with public access and shoals that give a paddler something to work with on the way to West Point Lake.
buzz: Good shoal water in spring and quiet the rest of the year. Outfitters are thin, so plan your own shuttle.

name: West Point Lake
unique: A 26,000 acre Corps lake on the Chattahoochee with standing timber in the upper reaches and campgrounds and coves on the Heard County side.
buzz: Bass and crappie fishing is the main use and the lake is big enough to find quiet water on a weekend.

name: Heard County Courthouse and Franklin Square
unique: A county seat incorporated in 1831 with a courthouse square on the road to the river, in the last county before Alabama.
buzz: Quiet and small, with the square as the whole downtown. A natural stop on the way to West Point Lake.

name: Talbot County Courthouse
unique: A Romanesque courthouse of 1892 on a square ringed by antebellum and Victorian houses, in a county settled in 1827 that produced governors and a vice president's family.
buzz: One of the best small courthouse squares in the state, and almost nobody stops. The houses around it are the real collection.

name: Talbotton Antebellum Streets
unique: A grid of 1830s streets with a concentration of antebellum houses that survived because the railroad went elsewhere and the town stopped growing.
buzz: The best houses are on the side streets and a slow drive or walk covers them. Respect the private yards and the dogs.

name: Talbot County Farm Country
unique: Rolling pasture and pine on the edge of the Piedmont, with cattle farms, old barns and dirt roads that look like the county did a century ago.
buzz: This is drive and look country, best in late light. No services, so fuel up before you turn off the highway.

name: Flint River at Taylor County
unique: The Flint runs the eastern line of Taylor County with limestone shoals, sandbars and cypress, water that clears up as it comes down out of the Piedmont.
buzz: Shoal bass fishing is the local obsession and the shoals are the reason. Water levels make or break a trip.

name: Taylor County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse on the square in Butler, the county seat of a county named for a president who died before the county existed, with Reynolds a few miles east.
buzz: A five minute stop between the river and the highway. The square is intact and quiet.

name: Butler Downtown and the Old Storefronts
unique: A small brick downtown around the square with a hardware store and a lunch counter that have outlasted the chains on the bypass.
buzz: The lunch counter is the reason locals stop. Twenty minutes of walk and you have seen the town.

name: Pasaquan
unique: Seven acres of painted buildings, totems and concrete walls built by Eddie Owens Martin, who called himself St EOM and worked on it for thirty years, now restored by a university.
buzz: The painted mandalas and the snake wall are the photographs. Restored and stable now, and still gloriously strange.

name: Buena Vista Downtown Square
unique: A courthouse square in a town named for a battle, with a 1930s courthouse, a ring of shops and the Pasaquan turnoff two miles out.
buzz: Most visitors pass straight through to Pasaquan and miss the square. A few minutes more is worth it.

name: Marion County Farm and Pine Country
unique: Peach orchards, pecan groves and pine on the fall line, with the Flint River forming the county's west line and dirt roads running down to it.
buzz: Peaches in June and pecans in autumn are when the stands are worth stopping. Otherwise it is a quiet drive.

name: Schley County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse on a square in one of Georgia's smallest counties, created in 1857 and named for a Maryland politician who never lived here.
buzz: Two minutes off the highway and the whole town is one block. The square is the photograph.

name: Ellaville Downtown
unique: A single commercial block around the courthouse in a county of under five thousand people, with the cotton warehouses and the rail line still visible at the edge.
buzz: Very little here and no pretence about it. A leg stretch and a look at the square.

name: Schley County Farm Country
unique: Cotton, peanuts and pecans on flat farmland with the pecan groves in orderly rows, in a county that has lost population every decade since 1900.
buzz: Pecan harvest in late autumn is the season to drive it. Otherwise it is a look at how the county still lives.
